newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore, Eritrea vow to develop bilateral links.
newsitem.headline: Singapore, Eritrea vow to develop bilateral links.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong held talks on Wednesday with Eritrean President Isayas Afewerki to develop bilateral ties between the two nations, officials said.
The two leaders exchanged views for an hour on ways to boost relations between Singapore and Africa's newest democracy, they said. The officials declined to provide details of the talks.
"My government intends to enhance and upgrade our bilateral relations," Afewerki said later at a dinner.
"Your visit to Singapore has given a boost to bilateral relations," Goh said in reply. "Let us work together to advance our common interests."
Afewerki, a guerrilla leader in Eritrea's long war to win independence from Ethiopia, paid a courtesy call on Singapore President Ong Teng Cheong and toured Singapore's teeming port.
He is the first Eritrean leader to visit Singapore.

Eritrea waged an often bitter 30-year war against Ethiopia which only ended in 1991. It became independent in 1993 and is trying hard to rebuild an economy wrecked by the long conflict with its southern neighbour.
